about.title: How the analysis works
about.how: Each position is searched by Stockfish running as WebAssembly in a Web Worker in your browser. The played move is compared with the engine's best move in the same position, at the same depth, and from the same player's point of view. If the played move is not among the top lines, it gets its own restricted search (go … searchmoves).
about.labels.title: Move labels ({version})
about.labels.text: Labels use the drop in the mover's expected score (0–100 points, derived from the engine evaluation). Thresholds: best ≤ {best}, good ≤ {good}, inaccuracy ≤ {inaccuracy}, mistake ≤ {mistake}, blunder above. Allowing an avoidable mate is always a blunder; missing a mate is at least a mistake.
about.accuracy.title: Accuracy ({version})
about.accuracy.text: per move, averaged over each player's non-forced moves. It is shown only after at least five scored moves and is marked provisional until the analysis finishes. Provider accuracy (when supplied) is shown separately.
about.brilliant.title: Brilliant moves ({version}, experimental)
about.brilliant.text: The idea: look at the position the way a player who calculates only 1–3 plies would. A move is brilliant when that shallow look rates it a clear mistake (at least 10 points worse than the best move at that depth), yet a full-depth search finds it is the best move, clearly better than the alternatives, sound from a depth beyond the shallow look, and still best on a deeper recheck. Without the recheck it is shown as a candidate. Because hardly anyone looks past giving up their queen, a queen-sized sacrifice only has to look bad within 1 ply, so a queen sacrifice followed by a quick mate can be brilliant. Engine depth is not human difficulty, so treat this as evidence, not a verdict.
about.great.title: Great moves ({version}, experimental)
about.great.text: A great move is the best move, far better than every alternative at full depth (at least 12 points of expected score ahead of the next move, and still clearly ahead on a deeper recheck), while a 1–3 ply look cannot tell it apart from the alternatives (it leads them by less than 4 points there, or even looks worse). An obvious recapture is far better than the alternatives too, but even a 1-ply look sees that, so it stays "best". It uses the same searches as the brilliancy check. A brilliant move is also great, but is shown as brilliant.
about.imports.title: Imports
about.imports.text: Chess.com: public monthly archives by username. The newest games can take up to ~12 hours to appear; paste the PGN for instant analysis. Lichess: by username, or by game URL immediately after a game ends. Only finished standard-chess games are analysed.
